clue.text: Australian mate who works the soil?

definitions.meaning: in Australian slang a ... is a friend or comrade, originally a soldier
someone who turns over earth with a spade

explanation.surface: A question about a friend from Down Under who tills the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a pal, from the trench soldiers, and literally a person who excavates earth.

clue.text: Leave city in protection of attorney and politician

indicators.note: the city sits inside, sheltered by, the attorney's letters

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, the American prosecutor
EC is the postcode for the City of London
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone flees town under the guard of a lawyer and an MP.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London's postcode is a standard crossword source for 'city'; 'in protection of' means held within.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear off from a place suddenly is a synonym of leave, used as a verb.

clue.text: Everyone was out in this officer's three-wheeler

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer, with the possessive S
a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: A puzzle about who joined a walkout, pinned on a commander's tricycle.
explanation.definitionFit: In a nationwide stoppage all workers down tools, so everyone is out, as Britain saw in 1926.

clue.text: Stone carved by mere lad

indicators.note: a carved stone is reshaped, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rock sculpted by an ordinary boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A green beryl prized as a precious gem, an example of a stone.

clue.text: Name of dog that is following girl

indicators.note: the abbreviation comes after the word for a girl

parts.note: lass is a Scottish and northern word for a girl
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to call a puppy that trails after a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The collie heroine of the films and TV series is a famous canine name.

clue.text: Continue to play a part in area of London

definitions.meaning: to go on acting a role

explanation.surface: An actor keeps performing in a part of the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase for keeping on performing, and a west London suburb with many stations named after it.

clue.text: One thousand gathering round SE resort

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the compass abbreviation
the letters are collected together into a new heap, rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written, south-east

explanation.surface: A crowd of a thousand assembles around a seaside town in the south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' is the anagram signal, not part of the definition; 'round' wraps the scrambled thousand around the compass letters, and 'SE' does double duty in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An Essex seaside town east of London with a famously long pier, a classic holiday spot.

clue.text: Former model in show

parts.note: ex- means former
to model is to sit or pose for an artist

explanation.surface: An ex-model appears in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal or uncover something is a synonym of show, as a verb.

clue.text: What's inside will make you happy

definitions.meaning: the stuff contained in something, a noun

explanation.surface: A promise that the contents of a package will please you.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is the material held within; as an adjective it means satisfied.

clue.text: One persecuting people in the hills of Devon

indicators.note: the word for people sits between the two hills

parts.note: tors are rocky hilltops on Dartmoor in Devon; plural, two of them
men means people

explanation.surface: Someone harassing walkers in the West Country uplands.
explanation.walkthrough: Hills are plural, so two TORs appear, with MEN between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is someone who torments, that is, who harasses or persecutes.

clue.text: Card displayed by strumpet

indicators.note: the answer is on show within the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A prostitute shows a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: A card of the suit that beats all others in a hand of bridge or whist.

clue.text: Woman mother has to show round

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: turned round, so the word for show is read backwards

parts.note: to air something is to show it in public

explanation.surface: A woman's mum has to demonstrate something to people around.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: Managed guerrilla's farms across the Atlantic

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
Che Guevara the guerrilla leader, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A rebel's farms in the Americas were run by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Large American cattle-raising farms, so farms as seen from Britain across the ocean.

clue.text: Boy changing name is a heart-throb

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy who switches his name becomes a pin-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' scrambles only 'name is'; 'a' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who charms women and is popular with them, a sense close to a heart-throb.

clue.text: Appliance repaired in Cheam

indicators.note: put back together differently, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A household device fixed in Cheam, a Surrey suburb of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Any mechanical device, a washing machine being an everyday appliance.

clue.text: Say nothing in prison

explanation.surface: Advice to keep quiet while behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to fall silent and to be confined, as in a cell.

clue.text: A rise, too

parts.note: a swell is a rise, as in the sea or ground

explanation.surface: A terse note that something goes up as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means also or in addition, the same as too.

clue.text: Son in a stew, finding place with Internet connection

indicators.note: the son's letter goes inside the dish

parts.note: Lancashire hotpot is a British meat and potato stew

explanation.surface: A boy in trouble finds somewhere to go online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a stew' looks like the idiom for being agitated, but it is a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A public area offering wireless access to the web, such as a cafe with wifi.

clue.text: Great Russian ruler, favourite with our sovereign

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A tsar is the favourite of the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter the Great was the tsar who modernised Russia.

clue.text: Mongrel likely to snap?

explanation.surface: A mixed-breed dog might bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid animal is a mix of breeds, and an irritable person may snap at others.

clue.text: Dance that will inspire some trendies for a start

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A dance that should motivate some fashionable people.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1960s dance popularised by Chubby Checker, an example of a dance.

clue.text: New version of book about children

parts.note: re means about or concerning
issue means offspring

explanation.surface: A fresh edition of a book on childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A republished edition of a book is called by this term.

clue.text: Attempt by American writer to produce verse

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: An American author's effort to produce poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Poems collectively; verse is a synonym for that literary form.

clue.text: Particular way to deal with three blind mice?

definitions.meaning: a single item or fact, a noun

definitions.text: way to deal with three blind mice?
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cuts off the mice's tails

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme question about handling three blind mice.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for an individual point, and cryptically the removal of a tail.
